##### Session

At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text, sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a New conversation button. Each lane's tasks, and the questions of the Ask tab, have a conversation of their own, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so the figure is the spec lane's on the Spec and Chain tabs, a Chain prompt starting in the spec lane, the code lane's on Code and Freeform, and the questions' on Ask.
The figure reads "Context", then the number of tokens, short and extra small, muted: "850", "42.1k", "123k", or "1.2M", to a decimal place below a hundred of a unit. It follows each reply as the harness reports it. While the next prompt would start a new conversation, as when the project has none yet or New conversation was just pressed, it reads "Context 0". Its tooltip says how many tokens the conversation the next prompt carries on holds, or that the next prompt starts a new conversation.
##### Slice

Just left of the context figure sits the Slice toggle: a small ghost button with a scissors icon, reading "Slice", which shows as selected while it is on. It starts off. Its tooltip says what the prompt is sent as: while off, the prompt written as a spec, its references linking to the spec they name; while on, the prompt with the `piton slice` of each spec it references. Clicking it turns it on or off, and it applies to every tab, Ask included. It stays as it is across sends, tab switches, and project switches, as the prompt being written does, and the help text gives way to it as it does to the session controls.

#### Hidden Anchor

While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes, they'll be typing into a piton anchor with a userPrompt property, named after what the prompt asks for, as its naming says. It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope)

##### Naming

Each task and question is named by the harness, rather than at random, so its files, its snapshot refs, and its header say what it was for. When a prompt is sent or queued, the harness is asked for a short title for it with the prompt-title prompt of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), in a run of its own that keeps no session, as the notes and commit messages are, with a small model where the harness can be told one. It is 
The title becomes the anchor's name: its words, each begun with a capital letter, run together with nothing between them, keeping only letters and digits, as in ChatTitlesFromTheAgent, and cut at a whole word to no more than 40 characters. A name that would start with a digit is begun with Prompt. A name already used by a task or question of the project, in its history, its questions, or its queue, is given the lowest number from 2 up that makes it unused, as in ChatTitlesFromTheAgent2.
Asking never holds a prompt up for long: it is asked while the spec builds ahead of a task, and a prompt is saved, queued, and compiled once it has its name. A title that hasn't come back within 10 seconds, that the harness fails to give, or that leaves no letter once cut down, is given up on, and the prompt is named as before, Prompt_ followed by 16 random hexadecimal digits. A task cancelled while it is being named is saved under that random name. Until a task has its name, its header shows no
A name, once given, never changes, so everything that knows a task by it, the task sent to the other mode from it among them, keeps finding it. A task resent or sent to the other mode is named after the prompt it was sent from, its name without any number the numbering added, numbered as above, without asking the harness again, unless that name was a random one, when it is asked afresh.             Just left of the Slice toggle sits the model picker: a small ghost
            button reading the model the next prompt goes to, short, as
            "Opus", "Sonnet", or "Default", with a chevron, extra small and
            muted like the session controls. Clicking it opens a small menu
            above it listing the models the harness in use can be told, as the
            \@{HarnessIntegrationScope} says, the one chosen ticked, each with
            its full name muted beside it, and "Default" first, which tells the

            included, but Freeform, which passes the prompt to the harness as
            typed and is sent to the default; with Freeform selected the picker
            is disabled, its tooltip saying why. Its tooltip otherwise names the
            model chosen and says it applies to the next prompts sent.

            The choice is remembered for the user, per harness, as the
            \@{UserPreferencesScope} says, and stays as it is across sends, tab
            switches, and project switches, as the Slice toggle does; it
            starts at Default. A prompt keeps the model it was sent with:
            its hidden anchor records it, so a queued prompt goes to the model
            chosen when it was queued, whatever is chosen when it is sent, and
            a resend goes to the model it was first sent to. A Chain
            prompt\x27s steps all go to its model. A message sent to a running
            task goes to the model the task runs with, whatever is chosen. The
            help text gives way to it as it does to the session controls.

            Code, "Opus", "Sonnet", and "Haiku", given to it as
            `--model opus`, `--model sonnet`, or `--model haiku`; for Codex and
            OpenCode, the models their own configuration lists, given with
            `--model` or `-m` as each takes it. A model the harness refuses
            fails the run, saying so in the harness\x27s own words. The notes,
            commit messages, and prompt titles keep their small model,
            whatever is chosen.
/' $f

content.text:
I added a model picker to the chat input's bar, just left of the Slice toggle. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

**What the spec now says** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#model`):
- **Picker:** a small ghost button reads the model the next prompt goes to, for example "Opus" or "Default". Clicking it opens a menu of the models the current harness accepts, with "Default" first, which leaves the harness to use its own.
- **Which models:**
  - Claude Code gets "Opus", "Sonnet" and "Haiku", passed as `--model opus`, `--model sonnet` or `--model haiku`.
  - Codex and OpenCode list the models in their own configuration.
- **Where it applies:** every tab including Ask, but not Freeform, which always uses the default. The picker is disabled on the Freeform tab.
- **Remembered:** the choice is saved for you per harness and kept across tabs and projects. It starts at Default.
- **Each prompt keeps its model:**
  - A queued prompt or a resend uses the model it was sent with.
  - Every step of a Chain prompt uses the Chain prompt's model.
  - A message sent to a running task uses that task's model.
- **Small jobs unchanged:** notes, commit messages and prompt titles still use the small model.
- **Refused models:** if the harness rejects a model, the run fails with the harness's own message.

**Anchors the code should follow:**
- `ChatInputScope`: `#model`, plus `#hidden-anchor`, where each prompt records its model.
- `HarnessIntegrationScope`: `#harnesses`, for passing the model to each harness.
- `UserPreferencesScope`: its list of remembered preferences.
